questions.question: Explain two advantages and two disadvantages of a flat organisational structure.
questions.correctAnswer: Advantages of flat structure: faster decision-making (fewer layers to consult), better communication (less distortion), employees have more responsibility and autonomy (improves motivation). Disadvantages: wide span of control means managers may be overstretched, less opportunity for promotion (fewer management levels), may lack clear authority for complex decisions.

questions.question: Describe the difference between centralisation and decentralisation, and give one benefit of each.
questions.correctAnswer: Centralisation: decisions made by senior management at headquarters. Benefit: consistency across all branches/departments, senior leaders have the big picture. Decentralisation: decisions made by local managers. Benefit: faster responses to local conditions, local managers understand their market better, develops leadership skills in junior managers.

questions.question: Evaluate whether a large business should delayer its hierarchical structure.
questions.correctAnswer: Arguments for delayering: removes expensive middle management (cost savings), speeds up communication between top and front line, empowers remaining staff, makes the organisation more agile. Arguments against: loss of experienced middle managers, wider spans of control may overwhelm senior managers, demotivation of remaining staff (more responsibility without more pay), possible loss of specialist

questions.question: Full-Mark Response Evaluate whether a rapidly growing tech startup should change from a flat structure to a hierarchical one as it expands from 20 to 200 employees. <div class="
questions.correctAnswer: A grade 9 response will: analyse flat structure benefits at 20 employees (fast decisions, close team, innovation, shared ownership); problems at 200 (founder overwhelmed, inconsistent decisions, unclear accountability, communication breaks down); hierarchical benefits at scale (clear roles, span of control manageable, career progression); drawbacks (bureaucracy, slower innovation, silos); conclude: some structural adaptation is necessary but a full hierarchy may kill the innovative culture - a hybrid with light management layers plus cross-functional teams (matrix elements) could preserve agility while adding needed coordination.
